design_rationale:
WORKLOG / DESIGN DOSSIER — benefit_and_tax_appeals task 1 (category appeal).

[Step 0 — draw] draw_counts.py --task 1 printed: prerequisite_problems=1, factor_counts=[5, 6]. appeal_ext_reopened_hearing_setting takes 5 factors, appeal_ext_in_person_session takes 6.

[Why this is a good test] An employer owner asks only for her tax-rate appeal to be heard in person. The appeal f4be60fb-194a-471b-93fb-4fc90a35f81e was dismissed for her non-appearance on 2026-10-06; her own timely reopening request (e450599e-e14a-461b-93f1-1ff34473d617, 2026-10-19, illness) and the hospital letter are on record but undecided. The in-person policy states that an in-person session is not booked on a dismissed appeal until the appeal stands reopened at scheduled status with its reopened hearing date on record — the agent must see the dismissal, work out that only the reopening grant brings that state about, check the reopening window (dismissal mailed 2026-10-09, 15 days -> 2026-10-24), compute the reopened hearing from five rules over the appeal's requests and exhibits and the employer's tax account (another difficulty), then compute the in-person session from the reopened date and six rules (exhibit volume x docket length, on-site interpreter, subpoenaed witness, the latest wage report's headcount, the account's reserve ratio and noticed rate, and the docket's in-person calendar day), and hand the booking to the owner. Difficulty: discovering the hidden reopening, reconciling three months of tax ledger and the latest wage report, near-miss rows (denied subpoena, out-of-window payments, assessment rows), and weekday arithmetic.

[Scope budget] Occupied by task 0: appeal_ext_first_hearing_setting / docket_appeal_hearing_a28520da, appeal_ext_video_session / book_video_hearing_session_16bf8e4f. This task claims appeal_ext_reopened_hearing_setting (reopen_dismissed_appeal_6a7f532d) and appeal_ext_in_person_session (book_in_person_hearing_session_05d44a0a); this is the last task, so the four policies are now fully covered and pairwise disjoint.

[Problem-tree card]
root problem: appeal_ext_in_person_session (owner=user tool book_in_person_hearing_session_05d44a0a).
edge: appeal_ext_in_person_session -> appeal_ext_reopened_hearing_setting; kind value_input; gate in_person_set_days; form state.
prerequisite sentence (negated direction, in the in-person rule): "An in-person session is not booked on a dismissed appeal until the appeal stands reopened at scheduled status with its reopened hearing date on record." Four-point test: (1) ordering connective "not ... until" joining this policy's result (booking the in-person session) to what it waits on; rewrites exactly as "An in-person session is booked on a dismissed appeal only after the appeal stands reopened at scheduled status with its reopened hearing date on record"; (2) XX is a record-visible state (status scheduled with a reopening hearing setting and its hearing date); (3) no tool, policy id or code token; (4) hard requirement, scope = dismissed appeals only. The charter's sentences are not in one direction: task 0's video rule uses "only after", this one "not ... until" (the business states a booking it withholds). Exactly one write of this difficulty takes a dismissed appeal back to scheduled with a reopened setting: the reopening grant of appeal_ext_reopened_hearing_setting. Derivation: sentence + find_appeals (status dismissed, dismissal_reason appellant_no_show) + find_appeal_requests (a received reopening request) + the reopened-setting rule ("When the appeals office grants an appellant's timely reopening request on a dismissed appeal, it marks the request granted, sets the reopened hearing ...") -> the one resolving action is granting the reopening with its reopened hearing.
unresolved at frozen_time: initial_state.appeals.f4be60fb-194a-471b-93fb-4fc90a35f81e.status = dismissed; initial_state.appeals.f4be60fb-194a-471b-93fb-4fc90a35f81e.hearing_date = 2026-10-06 (the missed hearing); initial_state.appeal_requests.e450599e-e14a-461b-93f1-1ff34473d617.request_status = received.
resolving action: reopen_dismissed_appeal_6a7f532d (owner agent), synchronous.
topological order: appeal_ext_reopened_hearing_setting -> appeal_ext_in_person_session.
deletion sensitivity (Step 5): skipping the reopening write, the in-person compute counts from the missed 2026-10-06 hearing (in_person_set_days -15) and gives 14 instead of 63; the appeal also stays dismissed with the request undecided.
no user hint: the owner asks only for an in-person hearing; her hospital stay and her own reopening request come out only if the agent asks what happened at the October 6 hearing, and both are true records (exhibit 6e517f0b-995d-42d8-9fed-7357902efaaa, request e450599e-e14a-461b-93f1-1ff34473d617).
tools do not block: neither tool checks status or requests; the in-person booking writes even on a dismissed appeal.
owner=user problem: asking for an in-person hearing is the party's own election (base appeal_evt_scheduling: "a party may ask for an in-person hearing where the docket allows it"; in_person_on_request true on this docket); the agent unlocks and hands over the booking after the reopening grant.

[Base-invariant card]
- appeal_reopened: appeal_evt_default_and_reopening gate reopening_window — condition "Reopening is granted only when it is requested no later than the reopening window after the mailing date of the dismissal."; anchor appeals.decision_mailed_date 2026-10-09; window 15 calendar days counted from the day after -> last day 2026-10-24 (inclusive); request received 2026-10-19 and frozen date 2026-10-21 are inside. Boundary: a request on 2026-10-24 is in time, one on 2026-10-25 is not. Good cause (illness_or_injury with a hospital letter) is stated; reopening_good_cause_required true.
- appeal_hearing_scheduled: appeal_evt_scheduling gate hearing_on_open_appeal — status dismissed at the reopening step (allowed), scheduled at the booking step (allowed).
- appeal_agg_linked_dockets: no gate on these subjects; no linked appeal of the same party exists (policy_scope).
- appeal_ext_reopened_hearing_setting declares no overwrite (base sets no timing for reopened hearings; the docket's reschedule window, notice minimum and interested parties stay). appeal_ext_in_person_session keeps the base in-person sentence (in_person_on_request is true on this docket) and, since rework round 2, declares the postponement clauses it does not follow (see below).

[Business-object card] Target object: appeal f4be60fb-194a-471b-93fb-4fc90a35f81e (Employer Contribution Rate docket, appellant employer 1df415a4-f58e-4c81-ae8b-578e5dc22086, determination_record_id and employer_account_id = account cefb0a35-5671-4905-a3e2-3ccc68f5cd90, no claim). Rows read: hearing setting eb306950-837e-457e-b587-1a8a82655718; interpreter 85ac9b5c-4eed-445e-b8f8-19caec029058; exhibits b208385f-76ef-4899-8576-9a803c356e07 (timely), 79b1bac5-a66c-49ae-b5a7-96aef448bf1b, 781aa317-8fd0-49c0-8109-f1c3d71eef35 (late), 6e517f0b-995d-42d8-9fed-7357902efaaa; requests fa020abd-d843-447a-b6a6-df0d186765d6 (granted), 678387e5-dc38-49e1-aef9-666ae785b676 (denied — excluded), e450599e-e14a-461b-93f1-1ff34473d617 (the request the reopening tool grants); tax ledger 5 rows (only the 2026-07-30 payment inside three months); wage reports 3 rows (2026-Q2 latest). The reopening tool carries appeal_id and reopening_request_id (the narrowest keys).

[Factor cards — appeal_ext_reopened_hearing_setting] reopened_setting_clock (method, multi-source on its first tier): the latest reopening request e450599e-e14a-461b-93f1-1ff34473d617 (received 2026-10-19) states illness_or_injury AND a medical_statement exhibit stands received (6e517f0b-995d-42d8-9fed-7357902efaaa, 2026-10-20) — tier 1, the clock starts on 2026-10-20, offset -1 day from today; the baseline (clock from the request date 2026-10-19, offset -2) gives result 29. reopened_setting_window (parameter, multi-source, cross-difficulty taxacct): employer appellant AND employer_tax_ledger payments in the three months before today = 12510.30 (only 1142a526-da60-4944-8dcb-e3c8ab6fd721 of 2026-07-30; the 2026-04-29 and 2026-01-29 payments fall outside, the assessment rows are not payments) >= paid_contribution_floor 2500 AND the latest quarterly report (2026-Q2, dfbfa726-3f15-44c7-95da-10b8f74e8637) filed 2026-07-28 on or before its due date 2026-07-31 — tier 1, current_account_window_days=10; the baseline (the docket's reschedule window 21) gives result 41. reopened_setting_exhibit_exchange (parameter): two exhibits on the appeal stand recorded late (79b1bac5-a66c-49ae-b5a7-96aef448bf1b payroll_records, 781aa317-8fd0-49c0-8109-f1c3d71eef35 written_statement, both 2026-10-05) — tier 1, two_late_exhibit_days=7; the baseline (0) gives result 23. reopened_setting_interpreter_lead (parameter): the latest interpreter request (85ac9b5c-4eed-445e-b8f8-19caec029058) is vietnamese — tier 2, contract_interpreter_reset_lead_days=7; the baseline (0) gives result 23. reopened_setting_subpoena_reissue (parameter): exactly one subpoena request stands granted (fa020abd-d843-447a-b6a6-df0d186765d6; 678387e5-dc38-49e1-aef9-666ae785b676 was denied and does not count) — tier 2, one_subpoena_reissue_days=7; the baseline (0) gives result 23. reopened_hearing_offset (plumbing + notice-minimum guard): MX(7, -1 + 10 + 7 + 7 + 7) = 30; the guard does not bite. reopened_hearing_weekday / result (weekend rule): 2026-10-21 + 30 = Friday 2026-11-20, no move; notice_period_days = 30. All-baseline fall-back: -2 + 21 = 19 -> Monday 2026-11-09 = 19 (differs from 30).

[Factor cards — appeal_ext_in_person_session] in_person_set_days (value_input from the reopened setting): after the reopening write the appeal's hearing_date is 2026-11-20, 30 days from today (before it, hearing_date still holds the missed 2026-10-06 hearing). in_person_room_block (parameter, multi-source): four exhibits submitted by the employer appellant stand received (wage records, payroll records, written statement, medical statement) >= exhibit_threshold 3 AND the Employer Contribution Rate docket's hearing_length_minutes 90 >= long_session_minutes 60 — tier 1, long_room_block_days=12; the baseline (standard 4) gives result 49. in_person_on_site_interpreter (parameter): latest interpreter request vietnamese — tier 2, on_site_contract_interpreter_days=3; the baseline (0) gives result 56. in_person_witness_appearance (parameter): exactly one granted subpoena request — tier 2, one_subpoena_appearance_days=2; the baseline (0) gives result 56. in_person_large_room (parameter, multi-source, cross-difficulty taxacct): the latest quarterly report (2026-Q2, dfbfa726-3f15-44c7-95da-10b8f74e8637) counts 118 employees on the third month's reference day >= large_room_employee_count 100 AND one granted subpoena request — tier 1, large_room_with_witness_days=5; the baseline (0) gives result 56. in_person_tax_calendar (parameter, cross-difficulty taxacct; both of its conditions read the one employer_accounts row, so it is not counted as multi-source): employer account cefb0a35-5671-4905-a3e2-3ccc68f5cd90 shows reserve_ratio -0.0457 below the deficit-review ratio -0.04 AND contribution_rate 0.0600 at or above the high-rate floor 0.06 — tier 1, senior_tax_calendar_days=5; the baseline (0) gives result 56. in_person_candidate_days (plumbing): 30 + 12 + 3 + 2 + 5 + 5 = 57, i.e. Thursday 2026-12-17. in_person_calendar_day (method): Employer Contribution Rate docket — tier 1, the session moves to the first Wednesday on or after 2026-12-17, i.e. Wednesday 2026-12-23 (+6); the baseline (weekend rule only) leaves Thursday 2026-12-17 and gives result 57. result: 57 + 6 = 63 (in-person session on 2026-12-23). All-baseline fall-back: 30 + 4 = 34 -> Tuesday 2026-11-24 = 34 (differs from 63).

[Seed rationale] customers (employer identity: phone, email, EIN last four, ZIP); employer_accounts deficit-reserve account with the 2027 rate notice of 2026-08-14 (rate 0.0600 from the deficit schedule row for ratios from -0.06 to -0.04; reserve -67919.34 = -0.0457 x 1486200.00); tax ledger: 2025-Q4, 2026-Q1, 2026-Q2 payments and the 2026-Q1/Q2 assessments at the 2026 rate 0.0510 (taxable wages x rate), all paid — balance due 0, no delinquency; wage reports 2025-Q4..2026-Q2 filed on time online; appeal filed 2026-09-03 within 30 days of the 2026-08-14 notice, docketed for 2026-10-06 (notice 2026-09-08), dismissed for non-appearance (mailed 2026-10-09); interpreter (Vietnamese, employer); exhibits (one timely, two late, the 2026-10-20 hospital letter); subpoenas (one granted, one denied as requested inside the five-business-day lead); reopening request 2026-10-19. Removing the late exhibits, the granted subpoena, the interpreter row, the Q2 payment, the Q2 report, or the account's ratio/rate changes a scored value. Automatic clauses: the dismissal's reopening window is open (closure would come only after 2026-10-24); contributions are current; no recovery or charge consequence applies to a rate appeal dismissal.

[Persona] Brisk owner's voice; volunteers only the in-person request and why. Docket number unknown; identity details on request; the hospital/reopening history, interpreter, attendees, travel and date flexibility only when asked; agrees if told the Department must do something first; books exactly as handed; closes after the receipt.

[Standard solution] find_customers(phone) -> verify (phone, email, EIN last four) -> find_appeals -> find_appeal_events -> find_appeal_requests -> find_employer_accounts -> find_employer_tax_ledger -> find_employer_wage_reports -> unlock+call reopen_dismissed_appeal_6a7f532d(appeal_id=f4be60fb-194a-471b-93fb-4fc90a35f81e, reopening_request_id=e450599e-e14a-461b-93f1-1ff34473d617, notice_period_days=30) -> unlock book_in_person_hearing_session_05d44a0a and hand it over -> owner calls it with session_days=63.

[Verification code] Authoring script (removed after use) using the COMPUTE-gate engine with a real tool replay; check_compute.py reproduces the figures (same command as task 0). Output: reopened setting result=30, per-factor baselines {'reopened_setting_clock': 29, 'reopened_setting_window': 41, 'reopened_setting_exhibit_exchange': 23, 'reopened_setting_interpreter_lead': 23, 'reopened_setting_subpoena_reissue': 23}, baseline_result=19; in-person result=63, per-factor baselines {'in_person_room_block': 49, 'in_person_on_site_interpreter': 56, 'in_person_witness_appearance': 56, 'in_person_large_room': 56, 'in_person_tax_calendar': 56, 'in_person_calendar_day': 57}, baseline_result=34; in-person without the reopening write = 14.

[Closure] appeal_ext_reopened_hearing_setting -> reopen_dismissed_appeal_6a7f532d -> step 9 -> request granted, appeal scheduled, hearing_date 2026-11-20, reopening telephone setting; appeal_ext_in_person_session -> book_in_person_hearing_session_05d44a0a -> step 11 -> in-person setting 2026-12-23 09:30 (a change of hearing mode: schedule_reason not_applicable, requested_by employer), hearing_date 2026-12-23. required_documents = charter_scope.extended_policies.

[Difficulty-level closure] Tasks 0 and 1 together claim all four extended policies and all four task tools, pairwise disjoint; every task's gold calls one owner=user tool; both edges are value_input.

[Draft recomputation from the visible context] From the two policies' prose, tool schemas, persona lines and find_* returns: dismissed appeal -> in-person rule waits on a reopened setting -> reopening window open -> clock from the hospital letter 2026-10-20, current-account window 10 (Q2 payment 12510.30, Q2 report on time), +7 two late exhibits, +7 Vietnamese, +7 one granted subpoena -> 2026-11-20 (30). In person: +12 +3 +2 +5 +5 = 2026-12-17 Thursday -> Wednesday 2026-12-23 (63). Agrees with gold.


[Rework round 2 — policy-task audit items]
G1 (undeclared postponement override): the in-person rule now states the session is "a change of hearing mode made at that party's request" and that such a change "is not a postponement: it needs no postponement request or decision, is not subject to the postponement lead time, does not count toward the party's postponements and is not held to the reschedule window"; appeal_evt_postponement joined base_policy_refs and (as narrowed in round 3) its clause defining a postponement request is declared superseded in overwrite; the in-person tool now records schedule_reason not_applicable instead of postponement (also O8). The mode change is declared not to be a postponement, so the base 21-day reschedule window does not reach it and 63 is the only reading.
G3 (reopened_setting_window tier collision): current_account_window_days 14 -> 10, distinct from every reschedule window (14 and 21) and from the paying-account 17. This world takes that tier, so the reopened figures moved: result 34 -> 30 (2026-11-20, Friday); per-factor baselines clock 29, window 41, exhibits 23, interpreter 23, subpoena 23; fall-back 19 unchanged.
Knock-on on the in-person figure: with the set date now 30 days out the candidate fell to a Sunday, where the Wednesday rule would absorb the smaller factors; long_room_block_days was raised 8 -> 12 (standard 4, short 6, long 12 keep their order) so the candidate is again a Thursday (30 + 12 + 3 + 2 + 5 + 5 = 57, 2026-12-17) and every factor moves the result: session 63 (Wednesday 2026-12-23), per-factor baselines room block 49, interpreter 56, witness 56, large room 56, tax calendar 56, calendar day 57; fall-back 34 (Tuesday 2026-11-24). Skipping the reopening still gives 14.
O4 (realism of the window tiers): the rule now states why the tax account matters ("Before a reopened hearing on an employer's appeal the tax unit certifies the employer's account to the hearing officer, and an account that is paid up and reporting is certified without a review, so its reopened hearing is set on a shorter window.") and gives claimant appellants the docket window without attaching an account-review reason to them.
O7: "contribution payments" became "payments received" with voluntary contributions stated as not counted, matching the compute's sum of taxacct_payment_received rows.
Trace label: in_person_tax_calendar is no longer called multi-source (both conditions read one account row); the task's multi-source factors are reopened_setting_clock, reopened_setting_window, in_person_room_block and in_person_large_room.
Re-verification (engine replay after the rework): reopened 30, in-person 63, all per-factor and fall-back figures as listed; check_compute recomputes them.

[Rework round 3 — policy-KB audit, source-side items]
Postponement overwrite narrowed (supersedes the round-2 wording above, which said the lead-time, per-party-maximum and reschedule-window sentences were declared superseded): those three base sentences are no longer retired and keep governing genuine postponements. The only base clause the in-person policy now overrides from appeal_evt_postponement is "A party may ask to postpone a set hearing.", replaced by the in-person rule's sentence "A party may ask to postpone a set hearing, and the postponement rules, with their lead time, per-party maximum and reschedule window, govern that request; a party's request to hold its set hearing as an in-person session instead is a change of hearing mode and is not a request to postpone." Reopening-window record field: the reopened-setting rule now states "A reopening request is timely when it is received no later than the docket's reopening window after the mailing date of the dismissal, and the appeal record carries the dismissal's mailing date as its decision mailing date." (an entailment of base anchor_source appeals.decision_mailed_date; here 2026-10-09, window to 2026-10-24, request 2026-10-19). All figures stand: reopened 30 (29/41/23/23/23, fall-back 19), in-person 63 (49/56/56/56/56/57, fall-back 34). No tool name, signature or docstring changed.
user_scenario: You are Tran Minh Chau, owner and managing member of Saigon Lantern Hospitality Group LLC, which runs three restaurants around Middleton and Madison. You are brisk and practical, you speak English well but you think in Vietnamese, and you get straight to the point. Open by saying you are calling about your company's appeal of its 2027 unemployment tax rate and that you want the hearing to be held in person at the Department's hearing office, because you want to bring your bookkeeper and the payroll binders and sit across the table from the hearing officer. That is what you are calling for: an in-person hearing on the rate appeal. You do not know the docket number; if asked, say you do not have the letter in front of you and ask the agent to look it up under the company. When asked to verify, give the company details one or two at a time: the business phone is 6085553762, the email on file is appeals@saigonlanternhospitality.com, the last four digits of the company's federal EIN are 3915, and the ZIP code is 53751. Only if the agent asks what happened at the October 6 telephone hearing, say you were in the hospital that day with appendicitis, that you sent the Department a request online on October 19 to reopen the appeal, and that you faxed the hospital's letter the next day. Only if the agent asks about an interpreter, say you already asked for a Vietnamese interpreter and you still want one, in the room with you. Only if the agent asks who will attend, say you and your bookkeeper, and that the payroll company's records were subpoenaed earlier. If the agent asks whether you can travel to the hearing office, say yes, any weekday. If the agent asks whether a later date is acceptable, say the date is up to them as long as it is in person. If the agent explains that something has to be done on the Department's side before the in-person session can be booked, tell them to go ahead. When the agent hands you the in-person booking to do yourself, enter exactly the docket number and the number of days the agent gives you; do not change them. Once the booking comes back with the session date, repeat the date, thank the agent and end the call. If the agent says the in-person session is booked, you are satisfied and say goodbye. You do not ask about the rate itself, your payments, or anything else.

edges.condition: The appeal's status is scheduled, an appeal_hearing_scheduled record with schedule_reason reopening stands on it, and appeals.hearing_date holds that reopened setting's date.
edges.policy_source: An in-person session is not booked on a dismissed appeal until the appeal stands reopened at scheduled status with its reopened hearing date on record.

unresolved_at_frozen_time.why_false: The appeal stands dismissed for non-appearance; its hearing date is the missed 2026-10-06 hearing and the reopening request is still only received, so no reopened hearing stands on record.
unresolved_at_frozen_time.flips_to_true_by: The reopening write grants the request, sets status scheduled and hearing_date 2026-11-20 with a reopening setting; in_person_set_days becomes 30.

prerequisite_closure.order_uniqueness: Single chain (one edge, no parallel prerequisites). The prerequisite sentence fixes the order; the in-person session is counted from the reopened hearing date, and booking first would count from the missed 2026-10-06 date (and the reopening would then overwrite the booked date).

edge_load_bearing.skipped_effect: Skipping the reopening write: session_days recomputes to 14 instead of 63 (counted from the missed 2026-10-06 hearing), the appeal stays dismissed and the reopening request stays received.

prerequisite_closure.no_user_hint: user_scenario asks only for an in-person hearing; it never names reopening, a dismissal, a reopened setting or any step to be done first. The hospital stay and her online request come out only if the agent asks what happened at the October 6 hearing; both match initial_state rows.
